info.title: Super Bar — integrated API reference
info.description: Single-file, code-derived reference for the HTTP API subset used by Super Bar: Deye, LG ThinQ, TCL and Tuya. Each operation selects its own actual service origin; paths have no artificial vendor prefixes. This is not a complete vendor contract or distribution permission. No credentials or embedded signing keys are included. Tuya RPC signatures, TCL SaaS signatures and AWS SigV4 require an authorized signing-aware client; Swagger UI alone does not produce them. BLUETTI uses BLE and has no HTTP operations here.

tags.name: Deye
tags.description: Code-derived documentation of the HTTP requests consumed by Super Bar, based on its current native Swift client. This is not an official or complete Deye API contract and is distinct from the vendor developer OpenAPI product. Response schemas describe fields used by the decoder; unmodeled fields are allowed and optional fields are not promises of server availability. Obtain the appropriate authorization for any use of these services. No account data, tokens, passwords, password hashes or actual device identifiers are bundled.

tags.name: LG ThinQ
tags.description: Code-derived inventory of HTTP requests used by the shared macOS/iOS LG client. This is not a complete or vendor-issued ThinQ contract. Response schemas document fields consumed by the client and remain open where device profiles or wrappers differ. No account credentials, API-key values, or real device identifiers are included. Obtain and supply your own authorized PAT and API access; this file does not grant service or distribution rights.

tags.name: TCL
tags.description: Code-derived subset of the HTTP requests and response fields used by Super Bar, not an official or complete TCL/AWS API contract. Documents current mobile-client interoperability behavior and does not establish service permission or distribution rights. Dynamic regional origins must come from validated discovery; placeholders cannot be used directly. No account data, passwords, tokens, access keys, signing secrets or fixed mobile application registration IDs are embedded. App-side Keychain storage, polling and UI are not HTTP endpoints. BLUETTI Bluetooth is outside this HTTP specification.

tags.name: Tuya
tags.description: Derived from the Super Bar Swift client, not an official Tuya OpenAPI contract or permission to distribute a mobile client. One real HTTP endpoint carries seven RPC actions; no synthetic REST paths are invented. Form signatures and RSA login encryption must be produced by an authorized client; importing this file into Swagger UI does not implement authentication. Credentials, signing keys and embedded app registration identifiers are intentionally omitted.

tags.name: LG Mobile
tags.description: Native Swift ThinQ mobile protocol: email/password sign-in, server-side SPX signing, OAuth renewal and model-driven ThinQ2 AC controls. Synthetic protocol tests pass; live account login is not yet verified. ThinQ1 and mobile energy history are not implemented. Secrets and application signing constants are omitted.

post.summary: Obtain or renew a session using query parameters
post.description: Actual current-client wire format: POST with query parameters and no request body. For grant_type=password, username is the account email and password is the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the entered password, not plaintext. For grant_type=refresh_token, supply refresh_token instead. OpenAPI parameter required flags cannot express these cross-parameter alternatives; see x-grant-parameters. The embedded client_id value is protocol metadata, not a private developer secret.

get.description: Uses AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 with temporary Cognito credentials, signing scope date/region/iotdata/aws4_request. Sign host, x-amz-date and x-amz-security-token; additionally sign content-type for JSON bodies. The signer SHA-256 hashes the body and separately URI-encodes the already escaped wire path (including percent signs). Swagger UI cannot generate or refresh SigV4 signatures from this declaration; send through a signing-aware client.

post.description: Uses AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 with temporary Cognito credentials, signing scope date/region/iotdata/aws4_request. Sign host, x-amz-date and x-amz-security-token; additionally sign content-type for JSON bodies. The signer SHA-256 hashes the body and separately URI-encodes the already escaped wire path (including percent signs). Swagger UI cannot generate or refresh SigV4 signatures from this declaration; send through a signing-aware client. The literal %24 encodes the $ in the reserved MQTT topic on the HTTP wire. A successful publish acknowledges transport only. The adapter polls GET shadow every two seconds for up to 32 seconds and checks reported values before considering a control command confirmed.

TCL_AWSSigV4.description: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Authorization generated per request by TCLIoTSigner from temporary Cognito credentials. Do not paste a persistent access secret here. No automatic signing is provided by OpenAPI/Swagger UI.

DEYE_NonNegativeNumber.description: The client accepts a finite, non-negative JSON number or a numeric string; booleans and invalid numeric strings are ignored.

DEYE_ErrorEnvelope.description: Optional provider error fields inspected by the client, including errors returned with a successful HTTP status. This is not a complete error contract.

access_token.description: Access token. A leading Bearer prefix, if present, is removed by the client.

DEYE_TokenSet.description: A usable login response must supply a non-empty access_token. expires_in is interpreted as seconds from the current time. No credential examples are included.

DEYE_Station.description: The client selects the first row and accepts id, or stationId as fallback, when it is a positive integer. Fields are optional here because this specification records the consumed subset rather than a vendor guarantee.

DEYE_SystemStatistics.description: generationPower is consumed as watts and generationValue as daily kWh. lastUpdateTime, or collectionTime as fallback, is a Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds; the client divides values above 1e12 by 1000.

DEYE_HistoryRecord.description: dateTime is a Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds. generationPower is consumed as watts. The client retains valid records belonging to the requested calendar day.

statistics.description: Daily generationValue is consumed as kWh.

DEYE_DailyHistory.description: The app queries year/month/day using Asia/Manila for its existing accounting model. This documents client behavior, not a vendor-wide timezone promise.

LG_DeviceProfile.description: Device-specific capability tree. The client recursively locates groups/properties, checks mode containing w, writable=true, or value.w/writeValues, and reads enum/range limits. Nesting and available fields vary by device.

airConOperationMode.description: POWER_ON and POWER_OFF are recognized by the client; other values remain unknown.

LG_ControlBody.description: Map from a supported capability group to property/value changes. Super Bar validates each change against the device profile, sends one group per request, and polls state to confirm it. A successful HTTP response alone does not confirm a physical change.

targetTemperature.description: Use the range exposed by this device profile.

airFlow.description: windStrength or windStrengthDetail, as exposed by the device profile.

LG_ControlResult.description: The client ignores the control response payload and confirms changes by reading device state. A zero-length successful body is also accepted.

property.description: The client recursively searches for this list and only requests usage when it includes energyUsage.

energyUsage.description: Interpreted by this implementation as watt-hours; only finite nonnegative values are used.

LG_EnergyUsageRow.description: The client accepts multiple date field names and takes the first eight numeric characters as the calendar day. Provider date representation and additional runtime counters remain open.

LG_EnergyUsage.description: The client recursively finds dataList. The desktop decoder also accepts result/total and several alternate aggregate forms; this partial schema leaves provider-specific wrappers and fields open.

deye.title: Super Bar — Deye client API subset
deye.description: Code-derived documentation of the HTTP requests consumed by Super Bar, based on its current native Swift client. This is not an official or complete Deye API contract and is distinct from the vendor developer OpenAPI product. Response schemas describe fields used by the decoder; unmodeled fields are allowed and optional fields are not promises of server availability. Obtain the appropriate authorization for any use of these services. No account data, tokens, passwords, password hashes or actual device identifiers are bundled.

x-client-policy.redirects: Authenticated redirects are blocked. Before login the app manually follows at most five public regional redirects and validates each HTTPS origin against the listed servers.
x-client-policy.credentials: The current app stores sessions and renewal password hashes in Keychain. Credential parameters on the token endpoint are sent in the query string by the existing client; never log or share those request URLs.
x-client-policy.history: Historical requests are read-only. Unavailable daily responses are recorded as missing data rather than zero.

lg.title: Super Bar — LG ThinQ API subset
lg.description: Code-derived inventory of HTTP requests used by the shared macOS/iOS LG client. This is not a complete or vendor-issued ThinQ contract. Response schemas document fields consumed by the client and remain open where device profiles or wrappers differ. No account credentials, API-key values, or real device identifiers are included. Obtain and supply your own authorized PAT and API access; this file does not grant service or distribution rights.

tcl.title: Super Bar — TCL adapter HTTP API
tcl.description: Code-derived subset of the HTTP requests and response fields used by Super Bar, not an official or complete TCL/AWS API contract. Documents current mobile-client interoperability behavior and does not establish service permission or distribution rights. Dynamic regional origins must come from validated discovery; placeholders cannot be used directly. No account data, passwords, tokens, access keys, signing secrets or fixed mobile application registration IDs are embedded. App-side Keychain storage, polling and UI are not HTTP endpoints. BLUETTI Bluetooth is outside this HTTP specification.

tuya.title: Super Bar — Tuya Smart Life mobile API subset
tuya.description: Derived from the Super Bar Swift client, not an official Tuya OpenAPI contract or permission to distribute a mobile client. One real HTTP endpoint carries seven RPC actions; no synthetic REST paths are invented. Form signatures and RSA login encryption must be produced by an authorized client; importing this file into Swagger UI does not implement authentication. Credentials, signing keys and embedded app registration identifiers are intentionally omitted.
tuya.x-credential-policy: No real credentials, signing material, private host names or personal device examples are included.
